explorer.sousTitre: The places that make Azour: viewpoints, heritage, nature — and where to sleep, eat and camp.

pratique.venirTexte: Azour is in the Jezzine district (South Lebanon), ~20 minutes from Jezzine by road. Park on the village square, right at the trailhead.
pratique.kiosqueTexte: On the village square, run by Azour's young people and guides: information, advice, bookings.
pratique.aucunContact: The information number will be announced here soon.
pratique.alentoursTexte: Jezzine, about twenty minutes away by road, gathers the region's restaurants. Ask at the kiosk: the guides know which ones are open on the day you visit.

reserver.sousTitre: Outings led by Azour's young guides. You send a request, the kiosk calls you back to confirm.
reserver.envoyeeDetail: The kiosk has your request. A guide will call you back to confirm the date and the price.
reserver.preteDetail: Send it to the kiosk by one of the means below — or read it out on the phone. A guide will call you back to confirm the date and the price.
reserver.erreur: Sending failed. Use WhatsApp or call the kiosk — your request is copied below.
reserver.note: A request is not a firm booking: a guide at the kiosk confirms it.
reserver.aucune: No outings are on offer right now. Come by the kiosk or call.

agenda.sousTitre: The trail race, village events and the seasons of nature.

apropos.texte1: The Azour trails are being developed by the Municipality of Azour and the Libanais en Yvelines association (LEY), with the towns of Villepreux and Jouy-en-Josas, YCID (Yvelines International Cooperation and Development), the Département des Yvelines and the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, within the CEM Lebanon cooperation programme 2025-2027.
apropos.texte2: The village youth cleared the first sections, are training as guides and run the kiosk. This app is theirs: its content is written and updated in Azour.
apropos.photos: Photos from the Azour trail study (2026) and the CEM Lebanon programme.
apropos.duplicable: This platform is built to be duplicated: any village can open its own, with its trails, places and contacts — without touching the code.
